audience.text: C++ developers building cross-platform applications that need to generate or manipulate PowerPoint presentations without requiring Microsoft PowerPoint or COM interop.

capabilities.text: Create new presentations or load existing .pptx files, add slides, and save in Office Open XML formats using the Presentation class.
capabilities.title: Create and modify presentations

capabilities.text: Add, remove, and clone slides; insert AutoShapes, Tables, Connectors, and PictureFrames; reorder shapes; and traverse nested GroupShapes.
capabilities.title: Manage slides and shapes

capabilities.text: Apply character, paragraph, and text-frame formatting; solid, gradient, pattern, or picture fills; line styles; and visual effects like shadows and 3D.
capabilities.title: Format text and shapes

capabilities.text: Add comment authors, comments, and replies with timestamps and positions; manage core, application, and custom document properties.
capabilities.title: Add comments and document properties

capabilities.text: Embed images from in-memory byte buffers via ImageCollection::add_image() and attach them as PictureFrames to slides.
capabilities.title: Embed images

capabilities.text: Save presentations to six Office Open XML formats: PPTX, PPTM, PPSX, PPSM, POTX, and POTM using SaveFormat.
capabilities.title: Export to PowerPoint formats

limitations.text: No support for charts, SmartArt, OLE objects, mathematical text, animations, slide transitions, group shapes, hyperlinks, slide backgrounds, themes, or slide size configuration.
Saving to streams, loading images from paths or streams, and exporting to non-PPTX formats (PDF, HTML, SVG, images) is unsupported and throws std::invalid_argument.
slides().add_clone() loses the source shapes' text; masters().add_clone() does not persist to the saved file.
pugixml is exposed in the public interface, requiring consumers to have its headers available; miniz is linked privately and only needed at link time.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic PowerPoint presentation creation and modification in C++ without external dependencies like Microsoft Office.
Provides a CMake-integrated build system with automatic dependency fetching via FetchContent for pugixml, miniz, and GoogleTest.
Supports preservation of unknown XML parts during load-save round-trips, ensuring content not yet modeled remains intact.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for C++ is a C++20 library for creating, reading, and editing PowerPoint .pptx presentations, distributed under the MIT license.

uncertainties: The exact set of SaveFormat values supported beyond the six Office Open XML formats is not fully enumerated in facts.
Whether the library supports VBA macro reading or writing beyond throwing on macro-enabled formats is not stated.
The behavior of add_clone() and insert_clone() for layout slides or master slides is not detailed beyond masters().add_clone().

workflows.name: Build from source
workflows.text: Clone the repository and run CMake to configure and build the library using CMake 3.20+ and C++20.

workflows.name: Consume via CMake FetchContent
workflows.text: Integrate the library directly into a CMake project using FetchContent, with include paths exposed via the aspose_slides_foss target.

workflows.name: Run tests
workflows.text: Build and run unit, integration, and conformance tests under tests/ using GoogleTest, with CI validating output package structure.
